_comment: Every matrix the pipeline fans out over, in one place, so `dart-test`,
`autocomplete-shell-smoke`, and `build-and-package` each keep one job
body and so the assets the release jobs publish can be compared against
this file in a test.
`host` is the primary Linux entry and `cross` is everything else. The
`changes` job currently merges both on every event, so a pull request
gets the same coverage as the merge queue: this repository's subject is
filesystem semantics -- symlinks, Windows junctions, path handling --
so macOS and Windows are not duplicates of the Linux run, they exercise
different code. The split is kept because narrowing a pull request to
`host` is then a one-line change to `matrix_scope` in that job.
macos-13, the previous Intel label, was retired by GitHub; macos-15-intel
is the supported Intel macOS runner.
`test` deliberately covers three hosts rather than all six package
targets. Every divergence this codebase has is an OS-flavour difference
(Windows against POSIX, glibc against BSD libc); the arm64 and Intel
entries in `package` re-verify architecture, which the FFI declarations
in lib/src/util/native_stat.dart and lib/src/util/posix_chmod.dart are
independent of. Revisit if either grows an IntPtr, a @Packed, or a
pointer-sized struct member.
